brief_corrections: Task 1 question 2: the premise is false - the region address IS recorded (as [d], the elements pointer = the region base) and the size IS recorded (as [d+8]); freeing at death is not blocked by missing bookkeeping
Task 1 question 5: "above 4,097 elements" is off by one element read strictly - a kosh with exactly 4,097 elements already has a region; the largest size without one is 4,096

Shared state: "81 gates" is right as a total (78 run_gate + X11 + doc_counts + Windows skip = 81 entries) but the reference status line's "81 PASS" is wrong (max PASS 80) - the same off-by-one as R159 finding P4, one gate higher

boundary.documented_as: past 64 KiB (bytes) only, in the reference and the memory-model doc; the books never mention regions
boundary.source: R127_BIG equ 65536 bytes (src/r65_arena.inc:571) compared against new capacity in bytes, with capacity doubling (4, 8, ..., 4096, 8192); the first region-taking growth is the 4,097th push
boundary.where_named: nowhere as a constant - a consequence, not a named threshold

task1.munmap_releases: the whole old region, both platforms (Linux: munmap(old [d], old [d+8]); Windows: VirtualFree(addr, 0, MEM_RELEASE)); the win/winrt_blob.asm:184 comment is accurate

per_dead_big_kosh.committed: at most 64 KiB at the boundary (R169 measured 68 KB resident per 4,097-element block); ~16 MB for a 2,000,000-element kosh

task1.pointer_recorded: in the descriptor: [d] is the region base (the mmap return becomes the elements pointer directly) and [d+8] is the region size; no side table
task1.reservation_site: one live place: r127_emit_grow's .big branch (src/r65_arena.inc:650-663); creation never takes a region (r101a_emit_kosh_alloc jumps to emit_nirmmita_from_rax)
task1.reserved_or_committed: reserved, not committed, on both platforms (Linux: MAP_NORESERVE; Windows: MEM_RESERVE only, rt_veh commits up to 64 KiB per fault)
task1.thousand_passes: 1,000 passes at the boundary = 64 GiB address space + ~64 MiB committed - the brief's arithmetic is exact; the program fails only under a virtual-memory limit (region mmap fails -> grow message -> exit 1)
task1.verdict: the brief's second premise is false; defect 1 is primarily an address-space leak

task2.block_entry: one stack slot per mandapa depth plus a rdtsc generation (r82_block_enter :10703); no heap allocation, no per-kosh allocation
task2.block_exit: drops the compile-time r108_bk_* record, zeroes the liveness slot, rewinds the scratch cursor only; never touches the persistent side
task2.leak_mechanism: the persistent cursor only moves forward; the only munmap is on growth; block exit touches no persistent storage
task2.sixteen_bytes: 24 bytes of R82 header (line + liveness slot + generation) minus 8 bytes of alignment padding the plain allocation already pays
task2.why_block_adds_it: r82_on is a program-wide flag (r82_note_kosh_decl :10662 sets it when any kosh is declared at r72_mdepth > 0); every kosh decl checks it (:19315)

task3.alive_but_thinks_dead: a function-scope kosh passed by its own name to a foreign function with a ptr parameter - the FFI door explicitly permits it (src/r32_ffi.inc:680-755), C receives the elements address via mov rax,[rax] (.ptr :740-755), and C may keep it indefinitely; no escape byte, no taint, no record exists
task3.dead_but_cannot_know: a kosh in a loop body, pushed once and read once, is dead after the read each pass - but the compiler has no last-use analysis and no (name -> storage) record
further_cases: inline asm can load a kosh's descriptor address and keep it (R148 shape 14, no check by construction)
aliasing is tracked only as names, not as shared storage
a kosh returned from a function is a known escape (r126_ret_kind), not a hidden one
the caps fail closed, not open (256-entry tables, walk budget, fixpoint overflow -> keeps)

known_at.block_exit: names end (R4 truncation), record dropped, slot zeroed; nothing about the storage
known_at.call_argument: four doors (r108_check_call for block koshes only, r126_check_untyped_arg, r126_check_builtin, the FFI door) plus the walk's doors
known_at.declaration: name, kosh-ness, capacity expression, mandapa depth and taint (for a kosh in a mandapa); nothing about escape, lifetime, or last use
known_at.return: r73_check_stmt refuses tainted values; r126_check_return enforces kind match via r126_ret_kind; the walk has no AST_RETURN door

task3.r73_var_depth: mandapa depth only - a name in a plain block, loop body, or yadi branch returns 0, indistinguishable from a top-level name, a parameter, or an undeclared name; only caller :13159 in r73_check_stmt
task3.symbol_table: dispersed - R4 list (names), kosh_vars (kosh-ness), r73_syms (taint), r108_bk_* (block kosh record), r126_kind computed on demand; no record links a name to its allocation
